Merindol
may-ran-dol'
n. (village of the Luberon in Provence; destroyed with its Waldensian population in the massacre of 1545)
Provençal Merindol, from a pre-Latin root with the Occitan diminutive; the village stands on the north slope of the Luberon above the Durance.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Merindol was a village of Waldensian settlers in the Luberon hills of Provence, part of a colony which had come down from the Alpine valleys in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries to farm land left empty by plague and war. In 1540 the Parlement of Aix issued a decree against the inhabitants of Merindol, condemning them in their absence and ordering the village razed and its people seized. For five years the decree was suspended while the king was petitioned. In April 1545 it was executed. The baron of Oppede, as president of the Parlement, led a force of royal and papal troops through the Luberon; Merindol and Cabrieres were destroyed with some twenty other villages and hamlets, men were killed in the field and in the churches where they had taken refuge, women and children died with them, and a number of the survivors were sent to the galleys. The estimates of the dead run into the thousands. The dictionary enters Merindol because this is the largest single massacre of Protestants in France before the wars of religion, it was carried out by a court of law in execution of its own judgment, and it is very largely forgotten.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a decree as a judicial decision or order; to raze as to demolish, to level with the ground; and a parlement as a supreme court of judicature in France.

expand to see more

DECREE, n. [L. decretum.] Judicial decision, or determination of a litigated cause; an order, edict or law made by a superior.

RAZE, v.t. [L. rado.] To subvert from the foundation; to overthrow; to destroy; to level with the ground.

PARLIAMENT, n. [Fr. parlement.] In France, before the revolution, one of the supreme courts of judicature.

EXECUTE, v.t. [L. exequor.] To perform; to carry into complete effect; to put in force, as a judgment or sentence.

SLAUGHTER, n. [Sax. sleaht.] A great destruction of life by violence; carnage; massacre.

Modern Corruption

Provençal Waldensian village destroyed in April 1545, with Cabrieres and some twenty others, in execution of a decree of the Parlement of Aix.

expand to see more

The corruption to be named is judicial murder on a national scale, and the dictionary insists on the judicial part. The destruction of the Luberon villages was not a riot, a pogrom or a frontier atrocity. It was the enforcement of a sentence passed in 1540 by a court of record, led in person by that court's president, and the court afterwards defended its act as law. “yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service” (Joh 16:2) describes the state of mind exactly, and the men who held it were magistrates and not fanatics.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the obligation to remember what is inconvenient to remember. The Luberon massacre is poorly known in comparison with Saint Bartholomew, partly because its victims were poor hill farmers with no noble patrons and no historian of their own, and partly because France afterwards had reasons not to dwell on it. The dictionary holds that the church's roll of its martyrs should be kept without regard to their rank, and that the obscure dead are exactly the ones a register is for.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek sphazo (G4969), to slay; Greek dioko (G1377), to pursue, to persecute.

Greek sphazo (G4969) — to slay, to butcher; “the souls of them that were slain”, Revelation 6:9.

Greek thusiasterion (G2379) — an altar; “I saw under the altar”, Revelation 6:9.

Greek latreia (G2999) — service, divine service; “will think that he doeth God service”, John 16:2.

Hebrew ra'ah (H7451) — evil, affliction, adversity; “Many are the afflictions of the righteous”, Psalm 34:19.

Greek dioko (G1377) — to pursue, to persecute; “persecuted for righteousness' sake”, Matthew 5:10.

Usage

"“I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God” (Rev 6:9) — the Luberon villages, April 1545."

"“whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service” (Joh 16:2) — the state of mind of a court of record."

"“Many are the afflictions of the righteous” (Psa 34:19) — survivors sent to the galleys, and the dead uncounted."
